28. rule

"The addition of halo acid or other unsymmetrical reagent to unsymmetrical alkene occurs in such a way that the positive part of reagent goes to the carbon atom having greater number of hydrogen atom and negative part of reagent goes to the carbon atom having lesser number of carbon atom." Example: 2-bromopropane HBr Propene I-bromopropane The major product is 2-bromopropane.

Mechanism: It involves the formation of carbocation and carboanion. The carbocation and carboanion are formed by the displacement of bonding pair of electrons toward more electronegative carbon atom. The positive part of reagent i.e. H + of HBr adds to the negative part i.e. carboanion and negative part of reagent i.e. Br— of HBr adds to the positive part i.e. carbocation.
